subject: A circuit diagram of the harp: a shedding source tapping a ladder of tuned wire modes on the left, summed with a mains line into the output trace on the right.
controls: wind: position — the source's tap slides along the ladder bus to the mode it locks, and that rung lights.
span: count — the ladder holds 4 rungs on a short span and 12 on a long one, packed closer as they multiply.
gust: shape — the output trace's envelope breaks into uneven swells as neighbouring modes cut in.
hum: scale — the mains trace under the sum node grows from a flat line to a 14 px sine.
reference: opxy/reference/README.md (MNMD FM STAT-style diagram + trace, linked there)
risks: The most literal and the most explanatory, so it's closest to a dashboard: a ladder and a waveform could be any synth. Controls fall cleanly into the encoder columns (structure on 1–2, trace on 3–4). LC symbols at 10 px rungs are near the 3 px detail floor at 12 rungs. The output trace is a P3-style oscilloscope trace and risks 'says nothing new'. No physical pylon on screen.
